title: Google Global Infrastructure & Network Tiers — Request & Control Flow
purpose: Contrasts Premium Tier networking (routing entirely over Google's private fiber) versus Standard Tier networking (routing over public internet to destination region).
routing_rationale: Premium Tier optimizes latency and packet reliability by traversing Google's private fiber; Standard Tier trades performance for lower egress costs.

nodes.label: Tokyo Client Browser
nodes.detail: User sending HTTPS payload destined for US datacenter.

nodes.label: Premium Tier (Google Fiber)
nodes.detail: Enters Tokyo Edge PoP immediately; rides Google private subsea fiber to Iowa (110ms).

nodes.label: Standard Tier (Public Transit)
nodes.detail: Hops across 12 third-party ISPs across Pacific; enters Google network only in Iowa (175ms).

nodes.label: Backend Compute Instance
nodes.detail: Workload receiving payload and responding to client.

steps.title: Network Tier Selection
steps.action: DNS resolves to either Global Anycast IP (Premium) or Regional Public IP (Standard).
steps.why_traversal: Premium Tier uses Anycast; Standard Tier uses standard regional IP routing.

steps.title: Transit Comparison
steps.action: Premium packet traverses Google fiber directly; Standard packet hops multiple commercial transit carriers.
steps.why_traversal: Premium Tier guarantees SLA, low latency, and zero congested ISP peering points.

scenarios.label: Standard Tier ISP Congestion
scenarios.root_cause: Third-party ISP link in California suffers packet loss due to transit peer saturation.
scenarios.diverted_path: Standard Tier requests experience 20% retransmission rate and latency spikes.
scenarios.blast_radius: Only Standard Tier workloads impacted; Premium Tier continues running clean.
scenarios.recovery: Switch project network tier default to Premium Tier in Cloud Console.

scenarios.label: Quota exhausted
scenarios.root_cause: A project or regional quota reaches its allocation limit.
scenarios.diverted_path: Requests surface elevated latency, errors, or denied actions.
